geometry.locator: arXiv:1410.3151 section 5.1, list of MC thrown-event parameters, "Surface Impact Position"
geometry.note: Confidence verified: a surveyed coordinate from a rank 10 source; the rounded value in a second paper agrees.
geometry.quote: Surface Impact Position: Uniform, random distribution inside a circle of radius 25 km, centered at the CLF (39.296918 N Lat, 112.908733 W Long).

method: Point at the latitude and longitude the Telescope Array Collaboration gives for the Central Laser Facility (CLF), 39.296918 N, 112.908733 W (arXiv:1410.3151 section 5.1, where it is the centre of the Monte Carlo impact-position circle). The rounded 39.30 N, 112.91 W of arXiv:2103.01086 section 1 agrees. A position marker; the facility is a small installation.
name: Telescope Array Central Laser Facility
notes: The paper says the CLF is "at the center of the SD array, equidistant from all three telescope stations"; the centroid of the 507 stations is 4.0 km south of it, so it is the centre of the three-telescope triangle, not of the station grid.

summary.plain: The laser at the centre of the Telescope Array that all three fluorescence telescope stations fire at to measure the air.
